name: Bicycle Crunch
description: The bicycle crunch combines trunk flexion with rotation and simultaneous leg movement, training the rectus abdominis and obliques in a dynamic, integrated pattern. The alternating elbow-to-knee motion engages the obliques more than a standard crunch and creates significant rotational core demand.

execution.starting_position: Lie on your back with hands lightly behind the head, shoulders off the floor, knees bent at 90 degrees.
execution.setup_instructions: Keep both shoulders off the floor throughout. The rotation comes from the torso, not from pulling the neck.
steps: Extend one leg straight while simultaneously rotating the opposite elbow toward the bent knee.
Alternate sides in a smooth, controlled cycling motion.
Keep the lower back pressed into the floor throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale with each rotation. Try to maintain a rhythm.
common_mistakes: Pulling the neck with the hands
Rushing through reps with poor form — go slow for greater activation
Lifting the lower back off the floor
safety_considerations: If neck discomfort is significant, reduce range or regress to basic crunches
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full elbow-to-knee contact or as close as possible on each side. Fully extended opposite leg.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Controlled — 1 second per rep each side
coaching_cues: Rotate from the ribcage, not from the neck
Keep both shoulders off the floor — do not rock side to side
